title: Spin order and excitations in the collinear kagome antiferromagnet Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$
authors: Jin Ding, Yang Liu, Feihao Pan, Yinghao Zhu, Yixi Su, Stanislav E. Nikitin, Ursula B. Hansen, Mechthild Enderle, Zhilun Lu, Linxuan Song, Yong-Chang Lau, Xiaoyan Ma, Enke Liu, Huiqian Luo
abstract: Kagome lattices host rich magnetic, topological, and transport phenomena owing to their geometric frustration and strong spin correlations. Here we present a systematic neutron scattering study of the kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$, which orders into a collinear $c$-axis antiferromagnetic (AF) state below $T_N =$ 551 K. An additional anomalous Hall effect (AHE) contribution beyond the conventional magnetization-scaling response is observed well below $T_N$ under an in-plane magnetic field $\mathbf{B} \parallel ab$. Elastic neutron scattering demonstrates that the Fe moments preserve their collinear $c$-axis AF alignment down to 1.5 K at zero field. Inelastic neutron scattering reveals a distinctive Y-shape spin excitation dispersion exhibiting a two-gap structure below 10 meV, likely arising from two nondegenerate spin-wave branches. Polarized neutron measurements further show that the low-temperature spin excitations are strongly anisotropic: the in-plane component $M_{ab}$ dominates while the $c$-axis component $M_c$ is nearly absent. Upon warming, $M_c$ gradually grows markedly but remains much weaker than $M_{ab}$ even at 300 K. We propose that the unconventional AHE originates from a nonzero scalar spin chirality induced by field-driven spin canting either in the static or dynamic configurations due to gapless excitations. These findings establish the collinear AF kagome metal Y$_{0.5}$Fe$_3$Sn$_3$ as a platform for chirality-driven AHE without spontaneous spin reorientation.
summary: This experimental study characterizes the magnetic ordering and spin excitations in the kagome antiferromagnet Y0.5Fe3Sn3 using advanced neutron scattering techniques. The researchers report a collinear AF state and observe an unconventional anomalous Hall effect. They propose that this AHE arises from spin chirality generated by spin canting, establishing the material as a model system for chirality-driven transport effects.
main_problem: The study investigates the spin order and magnetic excitations in the kagome antiferromagnet Y0.5Fe3Sn3, with a focus on understanding the origin of an anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in a system with minimal net magnetization.
main_result: The material exhibits a collinear antiferromagnetic state with highly anisotropic spin excitations, and the unconventional AHE is attributed to a nonzero scalar spin chirality induced by field-driven spin canting.
method: The research employs systematic neutron scattering (both elastic and inelastic) and polarized neutron measurements, complemented by transport measurements (Hall resistivity) under applied magnetic fields.
model_or_system: The physical system is the kagome metal Y0.5Fe3Sn3, which orders into a collinear c-axis antiferromagnetic state below 551 K. The analysis focuses on the magnetic structure and the coupling between spin excitations and transport properties.
key_observables: Spin excitation dispersion (Y-shape, two-gap structure), spin anisotropy ($M_{ab}$ vs $M_c$), anomalous Hall resistivity ($\Deltaho_{yx}$), and magnetic Bragg peak intensities.
important_parameters: Low temperatures (down to 1.5 K), magnetic field parallel to the ab-plane, and energy transfer up to 20 meV.
main_assumptions: The unconventional AHE originates from a nonzero scalar spin chirality induced by field-driven spin canting, even when the bulk magnetization is small.
figures_summary: Figures show raw and extracted polarized neutron cross sections ($\sigma_{SF}, \sigma_{NSF}$) across various momentum transfers (Q) and energies (E) at different temperatures (1.5 K and 300 K), confirming magnetic Bragg peaks and characterizing spin excitation spectra.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents magnetic structure confirmation via elastic scattering, details the spin excitation spectrum using inelastic scattering, analyzes the spin anisotropy using polarized measurements, and finally links these findings to the unconventional anomalous Hall effect observed in transport measurements.
why_interesting: The connection drawn between lattice geometry (kagome), magnetic frustration, spin chirality, and transport phenomena (AHE) provides a rich platform for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated magnetic materials.
